description: hyper v1.12.0 tests/server.rs (chunk2): chunked request bodies, HEAD/304, keep-alive, Expect: 100-continue, pipelining.

cases.name: post_with_chunked_body
cases.notes: serve() fixture, no reply queued (default reply). hyper asserts: one read(&mut [0; 256]) returns Ok (any length, so no timeout and no RST), then server.body() == "qwert". The serve() fixture's serve_connection().unwrap() runs in a spawned task, so the connection result is not asserted.

steps.data:
POST / HTTP/1.1
Host: example.domain
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

1
q
2
we
2
rt
0

cases.name: post_with_chunked_overflow
cases.notes: serve() fixture, default reply. The 17-hex-digit chunk size overflows u64. hyper asserts: one read(&mut [0; 256]) returns Ok (no timeout, no RST), then server.body_err().source().to_string() contains "overflow" (decode.rs: "invalid chunk size: overflow"; table 7.1 canonical text). The smuggled 'GET /sneaky' is not separately asserted by hyper: if the size were truncated to 3, the body would be "abc" and body_err() would panic, so the body-error assertion already covers it. Observed on the reference: EOF with 0 bytes (TestService fails, hyper writes nothing).

steps.data:
POST / HTTP/1.1
Host: example.domain
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

f0000000000000003
abc
0

GET /sneaky HTTP/1.1

cases.name: post_with_incomplete_body
cases.notes: serve() fixture, default reply. Content-Length 10 with only 5 body bytes, then shutdown(Write). hyper asserts, in this order: server.body_err() returns an error (any kind; mirrored by await_event, which blocks like the mpsc recv), then one read(&mut [0; 256]) returns Ok (no timeout, no RST). Observed on the reference: EOF with 0 bytes.

steps.data:
POST / HTTP/1.1
Host: example.domain
Content-Length: 10

12345

Observed on the reference: EOF with 0 bytes.

cases.name: head_response_can_send_content_length
cases.notes: serve() fixture. Reply: header content-length: 1024, empty body. hyper reads to EOF (read_to_string, which also fails on invalid UTF-8: encoded as the (?su)\A.*\z regex) and asserts: the response contains "content-length: 1024\r\n"; the first line is "HTTP/1.1 200 OK"; after skipping to the first empty line, that empty line exists and no line follows it. The last two are encoded as starts_with "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\n", ends_with CRLFCRLF and after_head len 0. str::lines() also accepts bare LF line ends; the case requires CRLF on the status line and the blank line (RFC 9112 requires senders to use CRLF, so only a non-conforming server is affected).

steps.data:
HEAD / HTTP/1.1
Host: example.domain
Connection: close

cases.name: head_response_doesnt_send_body
cases.notes: serve() fixture. Reply: Full body "foo bar baz", no headers. hyper reads to EOF (read_to_string, which also fails on invalid UTF-8: encoded as the (?su)\A.*\z regex) and asserts: the response contains "content-length: 11\r\n"; the first line is "HTTP/1.1 200 OK"; after the first empty line nothing follows (encoded as ends_with CRLFCRLF plus after_head len 0). str::lines() also accepts bare LF line ends; the case requires CRLF on the status line and the blank line (RFC 9112 requires senders to use CRLF).

steps.data:
HEAD / HTTP/1.1
Host: example.domain
Connection: close

cases.notes: serve() fixture. Reply: status 304, header transfer-encoding: chunked, empty body. hyper reads to EOF (read_to_string, which also fails on invalid UTF-8: encoded as the (?su)\A.*\z regex) and asserts: the response does not contain "transfer-encoding" (literal, case-sensitive in hyper; ci added here to check the intent: no Transfer-Encoding field in any case); the first line is "HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified"; nothing follows the first empty line (no body, no 0\r\n\r\n). str::lines() also accepts bare LF line ends; the case requires CRLF on the status line and the blank line (RFC 9112 requires senders to use CRLF).

cases.name: keep_alive
cases.notes: serve() fixture. Reply 1: content-length: 11 + body "foo bar baz"; reply 2 (queued in hyper after response 1 was read; the harness queue is equivalent): content-length: 8 + body "zar quux". hyper asserts only that each read_until (8192-byte buffer, 1 s per read) reaches a buffer ending with the body, on the same socket.

steps.data:
GET / HTTP/1.1
Host: example.domain

GET /quux HTTP/1.1
Host: example.domain
Connection: close

cases.name: http_10_keep_alive
cases.notes: serve() fixture. Both read_until calls use hyper's 8192-byte read_until buffer. Only response 1 is checked for 'connection: keep-alive\r\n'; hyper converts it with s(), which unwraps from_utf8, so response 1 must also be valid UTF-8 (the (?su)\A.*\z regex). hyper does not assert the HTTP/1.0 status line (enforce_version downgrade).

steps.data:
GET / HTTP/1.0
Host: example.domain
Connection: keep-alive

GET /quux HTTP/1.0
Host: example.domain

cases.name: http_10_close_on_no_ka
cases.notes: serve() fixture. Reply: version HTTP/1.0 (no keep-alive header), content-length: 11, body "foo bar baz". hyper reads to EOF (read_to_end, 1 s per read, so the server must close) and asserts: the bytes end with "foo bar baz" and do not contain "connection: keep-alive\r\n" (literal, case-sensitive in hyper; ci added here to check the intent). The not-contains check runs on s(&buf), which unwraps from_utf8, so the bytes must also be valid UTF-8 (the (?su)\A.*\z regex).

steps.data:
GET / HTTP/1.0
Host: example.domain
Connection: keep-alive

cases.name: disable_keep_alive
cases.notes: serve_opts().keep_alive(false). Reply: content-length: 11, body "foo bar baz". hyper reads to EOF (read_to_end, so the server must close although the request asked for keep-alive) and asserts the bytes end with "foo bar baz". Not asserted by hyper: the connection: close header that enforce_version adds.

The contains check runs on s(&buf), which unwraps from_utf8, so the bytes must also be valid UTF-8 (the (?su)\A.*\z regex).

cases.name: expect_continue_sends_100
cases.notes: serve() fixture; TestService polls the body, which triggers the 100 Continue. read_exact of the 25-byte interim response, then the body is sent and the connection is read to EOF (Connection: Close). read_to_string also fails on invalid UTF-8, so the rest of the response must be valid UTF-8 (the (?su)\A.*\z regex). Server body side channel = request_body event.

steps.data:
POST /foo HTTP/1.1
Host: example.domain
Expect: 100-continue
Content-Length: 5
Connection: Close
hello

steps.data:

cases.name: expect_continue_waits_for_body_poll
cases.notes: http1::Builder::new() defaults (no timer) with a custom service_fn: asserts req.headers()["expect"] == "100-continue" (enforced: the service fn runs inside the serve_connection future that the test awaits, so its panic fails the test), drops the request without polling the body, sleeps 50 ms (the test's own TokioTimer.sleep, not a builder timer), responds 400 with an empty body. Mapped to test_service with read_body false, delay_ms 50, status 400. The client thread is joined, so its check is enforced: read_to_string to EOF succeeds (EOF reached, valid UTF-8: the (?su)\A.*\z regex) and begins with "HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request\r\n" (no 100 Continue first). serve_connection(..).await.expect(..) is Ok: conn_close outcome ok.

steps.data:
POST /foo HTTP/1.1
Host: example.domain
Expect: 100-continue
Content-Length: 100
Connection: Close

cases.name: pipeline_disabled
cases.notes: serve() fixture (pipeline_flush off). Two replies, each content-length: 12 + body "Hello World!"; both requests in one write. hyper asserts: the first read (4096-byte buffer, 1 s read timeout) returns Ok(n) with n != 0 (a timeout, RST or EOF fails the test); then 'if let Ok(n) = req.read(&mut buf) { assert_ne!(n, 0) }': the second read passes on data, on a timeout, and on any error (RST included); only Ok(0) (EOF) fails. The test comments say both responses may arrive in one read or in two. Port, one step per hyper read: (1) read_once max 4096 with read_result "data" (no allow_reset, no allow_timeout); (2) read_once max 4096 with allow_timeout and allow_reset, and read_result in [data, timeout, reset]. Remaining deviation: a socket error other than timeout/RST fails step 2 in the runner, while hyper accepts any Err. Both read_once captures depend on how the server's two writes reach the socket (one read may hold both responses, then the second read times out), which made reference-vs-reference diffs differ in 8 of 12 runs when an earlier version of this case compared a read_once capture. Both steps therefore set diff_capture false: diff mode compares only whether each step passed or failed (and the events), not the bytes. hyper does not assert the response bytes or that both responses arrive.

steps.data:
GET / HTTP/1.1
Host: example.domain

GET / HTTP/1.1
Host: example.domain

steps.comment: hyper: if let Ok(n) = req.read(..) { assert_ne!(n, 0) }

cases.name: pipeline_enabled
cases.notes:
serve_opts().pipeline(true). hyper asserts both responses arrive in the FIRST read (4096-byte buffer), line by line (the two date lines are not compared), and that the second read returns 0. The regex mirrors the line checks; [^
]*
 is the unchecked date line. The final 
 is required because hyper splits the zero-filled 4096-byte buffer on '
', so the last segment equals "Hello World" only if the body's '
' was read.

steps.data:
GET / HTTP/1.1
Host: example.domain

GET / HTTP/1.1
Host: example.domain
Connection: close

expect.regex:
\AHTTP/1\.1 200 OK
content-length: 12
[^
]*

Hello World
HTTP/1\.1 200 OK
content-length: 12
connection: close
[^
]*

Hello World
